members.name: orb_sector_momentum_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents, grouped by sector (banking, IT, pharma, auto, energy)
members.thesis: ORB breakouts on stocks that are sector momentum leaders (highest relative strength within their sector over the prior 5 days) have 20% higher follow-through than ORB on lagging sector members. Momentum leaders already have institutional accumulation tailwinds, and the ORB breakout is the continuati
entry_long: is_leader == True (stock is top-2 in sector by 5-day RS)
entry_short: is_leader == True in downward momentum (bottom-2 sector rank = weakest stocks)
members.exit_stop: ORB_mid (midpoint of 15-min range) OR 0.4% from entry
filters: sector index trending in same direction as stock breakout over 5 days
weaknesses: 5-day sector momentum can be driven by a single large move on day 1, making the ranking stale by day 5; the momentum may have already reversed
Restricting to top-2 per sector across 5 sectors = max 10 candidates, further filtered by ORB breakout; signal frequency can be very low (0-1 per day)
Momentum leaders are often extended and near resistance levels, making their ORB breakouts more susceptible to profit-taking reversals
members.prior_art: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) cross-sectional momentum; adapted for intraday ORB entry on momentum leaders. Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) on industry momentum.

members.name: orb_plus_sector_filter_v1
members.thesis: Standard ORB (Opening Range Breakout) has a ~48% win rate. Adding a sector filter — only take the ORB breakout if the stock's sector index also broke its ORB in the same direction — increases win rate to ~55%. The sector confirmation eliminates stock-specific false breakouts: if the entire banking s
members.exit_target: 1.0 * stock ORB range from breakout level
filters: stock volume > SMA(volume, 10) on breakout bar
nifty50 direction aligns with breakout direction
weaknesses: Requiring sector confirmation reduces trade frequency significantly
Sector index data may not be available at 1-min resolution from Zerodha — may need to compute from constituents
On days when the entire market breaks out, the sector filter doesn't add differentiation
members.prior_art: ORB with sector confirmation — sector-relative version of classic ORB

members.name: orb_multi_stock_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE, sorted by ORB signal quality
members.thesis: Individual stock ORB breakouts have ~52% win rate, but a portfolio approach — trading ORB breakouts across 5-8 uncorrelated stocks simultaneously — improves the daily portfolio win rate to ~70%+ through diversification. When multiple stocks break their ORBs in the same direction on the same morning,
entry_long: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakout signals (portfolio threshold)
entry_short: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakdown signals
members.exit_target: per stock: 2.0 * ORB_range_15[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio_pnl > 0.3% of total capital
members.exit_stop: per stock: ORB_mid[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio loss > 0.3% of total capital
filters: each stock breakout bar volume > 1.2x 20-bar SMA
NIFTY ORB direction should match majority of stock ORB directions
bid-ask < 0.05% on all stocks at entry
weaknesses: Managing 5-8 simultaneous positions is operationally complex; monitoring, adjusting stops, and exiting all positions requires significant attention and infrastructure
The diversification benefit assumes low correlation between portfolio stocks; on macro-driven days (RBI decision, global event), all stocks correlate to 1.0, eliminating the benefit
Transaction costs compound across 5-8 stocks: total costs are 5-8x a single stock strategy, eating significantly into the per-stock edge
members.prior_art: Markowitz (1952) portfolio diversification; adapted for intraday ORB context. Similar to Khandani & Lo (2007) on quant portfolio approaches.

members.name: orb_index_aligned_v1
members.thesis: ORB breakouts that are aligned with the NIFTY 50 index direction have 15-20% higher follow-through rate than counter-index breakouts. entry_long: aligned_long == True (stock AND NIFTY both break above 15-min ORB)
entry_short: aligned_short == True (stock AND NIFTY both break below 15-min ORB)
members.exit_stop: stock_ORB_mid (midpoint) OR NIFTY re-enters its ORB range (macro support lost)
filters: enter between 09:30-10:30; aligned breakouts must happen in first hour
CORE FILTER — NIFTY ORB breakout in same direction as stock (alignment is the strategy)
weaknesses: Requiring both stock AND index to break ORB simultaneously reduces signal frequency significantly; aligned breakouts occur on only ~30-40% of trading days

On days where NIFTY breaks out but then reverses (false index breakout), the aligned stock trade also fails, and the dual stop (stock ORB mid + NIFTY re-entry) can whipsaw
members.prior_art: Elder (1993) triple-screen system (multi-timeframe confirmation); adapted for multi-instrument (stock + index) ORB confirmation. Crabel (1990) ORB foundation.
